- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.16 or lower) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to cap the peak — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.66 or higher) and model shows downward bias, increase forecast by 2–5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movements — apply a 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +0.27 and -0.11), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting next period.
